new_passages.l860_B2_lead_in:
l.860 (v1 l.809), C-28: 'Theorem~\ref{theo:universality_tori} rests on the ergodicity of the group generated by the $\Phi_i$; one sufficient condition for it is a spectral gap of that group's action, which the following result characterizes.' This is faithful, clause by clause:
- 'Rests on the ergodicity': the hypothesis of EGF.universality_tori_of_ergodic is IsGroupErgodic volume (torusAffineGroup A b hA). EGF.universality_tori_iff shows the ergodicity is also necessary for the L^2 model.
- 'A spectral gap of that group's action is sufficient for it': EGF.ergodic_of_hasSpectralGap (HasSpectralGap implies IsGroupErgodic, for a probability measure; volume on the torus is one). The gap is Bekka-Guivarc'h's notion, the absence of almost invariant vectors in L^2_0, which is item (i) of Theorem B.2.
- 'Which the following result characterizes': Theorem B.2 is (i) <=> (ii) for countable H, the named Prop EGF.BekkaGuivarchTheorem5 (spectral_gap_tori). The generated group is countable (countable_torusAffineGroup).
- The sentence does not claim that a gap exists on T^1, and it does not exist there (bgConditionII_dim_one with the named Prop), so 'one sufficient condition' is the right strength.
This resolves CHECK-1 finding 9.
new_passages.l871_last_sentence: l.871 (v1 l.820), C-28: 'This is the first sufficient condition of Theorem~\ref{theo:universality_tori}: `the group generated by $(\Phi_i)_{i=1}^p$ violates condition $(ii)$'.' This is correct. Theorem 3.5 (l.312) lists its sufficient conditions in the order: Bekka-Guivarc'h (no non-trivial invariant factor torus with amenable projection, i.e. not (ii)), then no periodic integer vector, then on T^1 a translation of infinite order. The paragraph has just proved the first one: not (ii), then a gap, then ergodicity, then the uniform policy ergodic, then Theorem B.1 (EGF.universality_tori under the named Prop). It no longer calls not (ii) 'our technical condition' of a theorem whose hypothesis is ergodicity. This resolves the l.870 part of CHECK-1 finding 7.
new_passages.l874_d_geq_2:
l.874 (v1 l.821), C-28: 'In particular, if $d\geq2$ and the linear part of $H$ is the whole $\mathrm{SL}(d,\mathbb Z)$, projections such as the one in condition $(ii)$ are never amenable since $\mathrm{SL}(d,\mathbb Z)$ contains a free group with two generators.'
- The d = 1 case is now excluded. That is where it fails: at d = 1 every group of affine maps satisfies (ii) (EGF.bgConditionII_dim_one), and the SL_1(Z) criterion fails (EGF.not_universality_tori_sl_one).
- For d >= 2 the claim is correct, but cited and unformalized, as C-28's finding records. SL(d,Z) leaves no proper non-zero rational subspace invariant, so the only non-trivial invariant factor torus is T^d itself. The projection there is SL(d,Z), which contains F_2 and so is not amenable. The Lean proves l.316's d >= 2 criterion by another route (EGF.universality_tori_sl), so nothing in the paper rests on the unformalized step.
- l.316 ('for $d\geq2$ ... (Appendix~B.2; ...)') and l.874 now agree.
- The new added_hypotheses item ('d >= 2 for the SL_d(Z) criterion of l.293 and l.821') is in both sentences.
This resolves CHECK-1 major finding 3.
new_passages.l881_B3_lead_in:
l.881 (v1 l.827-829), C-32: 'Theorem~\ref{theo:universality_sphere} rests on the ergodicity of the group generated by the $\Phi_i$, not on a spectral gap. For comparison with the spectral-gap results cited in Section~\ref{sec:universality_sphere}, we recall that a complex number $x\in\mathbb C$ is {\it algebraic} ... The set of algebraic numbers is denoted $\overline{\mathbb Q}$. Bourgain and Gamburd prove the following.'
- 'Rests on the ergodicity ..., not on a spectral gap': EGF.universality_sphere goes through universality_sphere_of_ergodic and has no gap hypothesis. At d = 1 no gap exists (EGF.not_hasBGSpectralGap_sphere_two), yet the theorem holds (universality_sphere at n = 2).
- Section 3.1.3 does cite spectral-gap results: l.333 cites bourgain2012spectral and benoist2016spectral. \ref{sec:universality_sphere} renders as 3.1.3.
- Algebraic now means complex algebraic, which is IsAlgebraic Q (equivalently over Z) of complex numbers. That is the notion of EGF.BourgainGamburdTheorem1.
- Theorem B.3 (l.885) with this Q-bar is the named Prop clause by clause, and its hypotheses can be met (EGF.bourgainGamburd_hypotheses_witness, su2Witness).
- Q-bar's only use is l.885. l.333's 'algebraic coefficients' of real rotations stays meaningful, since real algebraic numbers are complex algebraic.
- l.881, l.888 and l.891 now agree.
This resolves CHECK-1 major findings 1 and 2.
